comments.text: > Our findings suggest that 90% of American working hours are spent on tasks with little or no coverage from existing benchmarks. comments.author: CoolestBeans
comments.text: Following is my experience and constantly pestering my friends across the industry for anecdotes. It isn't even that AI moves the bottleneck, the thing it solves was never the bottleneck in the first place (except for certain narrow verticals). AI both can't and doesn't do your thinking for you and worse yet, it robs you of the environment where you do your best thinking about data structures, algorithms, organization, etc. Code. Of course we can do that in natural language, but it's hardly the right tool for the job. All this being said, I don't think AI usage will meaningfully go down in the long run cause it's a very powerful dopamine loop and tech companies are very good at making those. How many people report social media making them unhappy and how many people do you know who have actually quit? Or to paraphrase Jim Gaffigan, nobody says they eat at McDonalds, but the sign outside says "billions served". Somebody's lying (and it's not McDonalds).

stories.summary_ja: 主な議論点は、既存のAIベンチマークが米国の労働時間の約90％をカバーしていないため、実際の仕事でのAIの性能評価が困難だという点だ。コメントではベンチマークが高給与職のタスクに偏り、清掃やごみ処理など低賃金作業は人間に残ると指摘され、ソフトウェアエンジニアや弁護士は再教育が必要だと主張した。賛否については、AIが本当に仕事を置き換えるのか疑問視する声（「ほとんどの人が実際に有用なアウトプットを出していない」「AIはボトルネックではない問題を解こうとする」）と、AIが知的労働を解放して人間らしい作業に集中できる社会改善に寄与すると期待する声に分かれた。注目コメントとして、ソフトウェアエンジニアの80％の時間がステークホルダー間の意見調整に費やされるという実体験や、AIはドーパミンループのように依存性が高く長期的には減らないという指摘が挙げられた。

stories.summary_ja:
**主な議論点**

**賛否両論**  
一部は長期間見逃されたことにレビューの限界を指摘し、ファズzingや静的解析では検出が難しいと主張。一方で、適切なファズzingやモデルチェックで十分捕捉可能だと反論する声もあり、ツールの進化次第では将来的に防げるという見方も示された。  

**注目コメント**  
バグの根本は特定データ構造の境界チェック欠如にあり、人間がエクスプロイト primitive を考えなければ気づけなかったという指摘が挙げられた。同時に、自動化ツールが将来的に同様の問題を防げるかという議論が交わされた。

stories.title_en: I Love Software Rendering

comments.author: delta_p_delta_x
comments.text: This isn't software rendering, it's called turning off spatial anti-aliasing. You can still do that in the modernest of modern games. Software rendering went out of the window because the CPU tends to have other things to do whilst playing the game besides only multiplying 4x4 matrices, which was shifted to the shader cores of GPUs. The look-and-feel that the author is discussing including shadow and texture LUTs can also be done on GPUs by passing the tables in to shaders as constant read-only storage buffers; that is not specific to software rendering. It bears mentioning that many modern software renderers (LLVMpipe/Lavapipe, OpenSWR, WARP) are basically full D3D/OpenGL/Vulkan devices in their own right, including shader compilers. Also, modern spatial anti-aliasing works by multisampling within a pixel (or even neighbouring pixels) and taking the average, rather than filtering across singly-sampled pixels, which massively reduces the quality. Not to mention temporal and machine learning AA techniques including DLSS, XeSS, FSR, and all the TAA implementations in many games.

stories.title_en: What on Earth Is Dekton?
stories.title_ja: 地球上でデクトンとは何なのか？

comments.author: zebrafruit
comments.text: It’s interesting that the focus is on porcelain as a cooking surface but misses the biggest reasons for it displacing engineered quartz or granite for countertops. There’s a few factors at play here leading to the prominence of porcelain. For the induction cooktops, you can cut porcelain slabs to 6mm compared to your 3cm (sometimes 2cm) quartz and granite. This is also why you can use it for walls and floors. The thinner materials allow the magnets to actually function. The manufacturing process for engineered quartz is now being interwoven with silicosis through the legal system, leading to manufacturers marketing “low silica” quartz at a cost premium. This premium is closing the cost gap with porcelain. This is the main economic and legal reason as jurisdictions- Australia and maybe soon California look to ban these products forcing the market towards natural stones. If you’re then selecting from natural stones, porcelain is essentially used as printer paper for whatever stone pattern is desired, and given that people tend to want things that look like marble, this “ink” is essentially free for the manufacturing process, making the porcelain look like marble more than quartz or granite. Engineered quartz is also not a great exterior material, again yielding to porcelain.

comments.text: The article misses an important bit of context (imo) that low thermal expansion glasses like CERAN have been around for ages and anyone who’s used an induction or a glass top stove would be familiar. However you can now get completely hidden stoves that look like stone countertops. If you’re not in the market for a kitchen, or know anyone people who recently remodeled it’s reasonable to not know they exist. I don’t know anyone with one, and everyone in our town still has gas. The author doesn’t explain which one they were buying, but it seems like the latter? Normal induction glass top stoves are a unit that drops into the countertop so of course you get the glass included (because at the very least, it has the decal for the cook zones and controller built in). The invisible ones only come with the burners so you can custom fit the top. Looks like you can get them off AliExpress even. It seems like this is the point of confusion - the author thought he could go down to a glazing shop to buy some tough glass..? I suggest go and watch Huygens Optics series about CERAN: https://youtu.be/qi8jmEbWsxU

stories.summary_ja:
・主な議論点  
Dektonなどのポーセリンがエンジニアードクォーツやグラナイトの代わりに台所天板で使われる理由について議論が盛り上がった。主に挙げられたのは、誘導加熱用に薄く（6 mm程度）加工できる点、シリカ肺症問題による規制強化でクォーツのコストが上がっている点、そしてポーセリンは石目のプリント紙のように好きな模様（特に大理石調）を安価に再現できる点だ。さらに、耐熱・耐汚性に優れ、外壁や床にも使えるという利点も指摘された。

・賛否両論  
賛成側は「高価だが赤ワインや熱いフライパンにも強く、満足度が高い」という実際の使用感を挙げ、特にCosentino製品への信頼を示した。一方で懐疑的な側は「本当に必要か」「ガラストップの誘導加熱と混同しているのでは」と疑問を呈し、価格対性能のバランスや、隠し型コンロ（CERANガラス）の存在を見落としているとの意見があった。

・注目コメント  
特に洞察に富んでいたのは、低熱膨張ガラスCERANと隠し型コンロの話題で、著者がポーセリンをガラスと勘違いしている可能性を指摘し、Huygens Opticsの動画を紹介して誘導加熱用ガラスの基礎技術を説明した点だ。このコメントは、素材選びの背後にある技術的・法的要因を広く理解するきっかけとなった。

stories.title_en: JPEG XL vs. AVIF for web use-cases
stories.title_ja: ウェブユースケースにおけるJPEG XLとAVIFの比較

comments.author: theandrewbailey
comments.text: I've been using AVIF on my blog for a few years. My blog's image corpus is almost entirely videogame screenshots, and I keep the original PNGs so I can re-encode if better encoders release. Despite playing around with JPEGXL every year or so, AVIF images usually looked better (if only a little) at the same file size (vs JPEGXL). After reading this article, there's something to point to prove I'm not going crazy.

comments.author: Klaus23
comments.text: The question now is how much of AVIF's advantage comes from the encoder compared to the image format itself. If it is the encoder, does JPEG XL even stand a chance of catching up? AVIF will certainly receive further improvements, albeit at a diminishing rate.

comments.author: fngjdflmdflg
comments.text: >Animated image formats are dumb and animated JPEG XL is no exception. Video formats are better at video. They're built for it. They're optimised for it. Not just in terms of encoding, but also in terms of playback. This is something I've felt doesn't get enough attention when comparing JXL and AVIF. AVIF can be the replacement for GIF. ><video muted autoplay> is right there. >No, I'm not adding a demo. I don't want it on my server. Use video formats for video. I'm not sure if "Use video formats for video" is saying to use AVIF over JXL or saying to use AV1 over AVIF. If the latter, GIF-like animations have a different enough user expectation that it makes sense to have it as something different from regular videos. Even <video muted autoplay> doesn't encode the full expected behavior because GIFs are not expected to have controls like pause, play and scrub. And even if you hide the controls users will expect similar behavior when opening it in an image viewer or in a new tab. Images do not have controls so they fit better as an image, although maybe they need their own category. Also, I didn't realize how good AVIF was at progressive rendering. I don't think I knew it could do that at all. I think AVIF is the clear winner for the web, although it is still nice to have JXL for lossless. Somehow I feel that AVIF still hasn't gained as much usage as it should, especially now that it is supported almost everywhere. I think I see more webp than AVIF, and JPEG is still everywhere. Maybe now that JXL is out, developers will take another look? AVIF is supported by 96.35%-98.83% of browsers according to caniuse whereas webp is 97.18%-99.68% and JPEG is 97.28%-99.78%. I also didn't know there was another Rust JXL decoder separate from jxl-rs named jixel.[0] [0] https://github.com/awxkee/jixel

comments.author: PaulHoule

Once you see it you can't unsee it and it boggles my mind that people are still using it as an example. Granted, AVIF performs impressively for, say, a huge hero image for a blog where you're out to create an overall impression and people aren't going to look at it closely. JPEG XL と AVIF の画質・ファイルサイズ比較と、違いがエンコーダかフォーマットかという論点。アニメーション、プログレッシブ、ブラウザ対応、ロスレス利用も議論された。

・賛否両論（意見が分かれた点があれば）
AVIF 側は同サイズでやや優れた画質、プログレッシブ表示、ほぼ全ブラウザサポートを実用点と主張。JPEG XL 側はロスレスと将来のエンコーダ改善を強調し、AVIF のアーティファクトを指摘する声も。

・注目コメント（特に洞察のあるコメントがあれば紹介）
あるユーザーは「ビデオはビデオフォーマットで扱うべきで、GIF代替としてAVIFを使うのは誤解」と述べ、コントロール期待の違いを指摘。別コメントではAVIFのプログレッシブレンダリングを初めて知り、ウェブでの優位性を評価しつつ、ロスレスではJPEG XLの価値を認めている。

stories.title_en: RFC8950: Announce IPv4 with an IPv6 next-hop
stories.title_ja: RFC8950：IPv6ネクストホップを使ってIPv4を発表

comments.author: Isomer
comments.text: I don't understand why you can't have any protocol that can (potentially recursively) resolve to a layer 2 address as a next hop. v4 route with v6 next hop? Seems reasonable. v6 route with v4 next hop? Why not? v4/v6 route with a mac address as a next hop? Trivial. v4/v6 route with a DNS next hop? Could be recursively resolved to a v4/v6 address, and then potentially recursively resolved to a MAC address. I wouldn't recommend it, but sure. v4/v6 route with a netbeui name as a next hop? You appear to be mad, but I'm not going to be the one to stand in your way.

comments.author: petecooper
comments.text: https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc8950/

comments.author: Alifatisk
comments.text: I guess the point with this to facilitate usage of IPv6.

stories.summary_ja: 主な議論点は、IPv4 ルートに IPv6 ネクストホップを指定する（あるいはその逆）ことを許可すべきかという点である。コミュニティでは、デュアルスタック環境での運用を簡素化し、既存のルーティングインフラストラクチャを活用して IPv6 への移行を促進できるという賛成意見と、ネクストホップの再帰的解決がルーティングループやセキュリティ問題を引き起こす可能性があり、既にトンネリングや NAT64 などの仕組みで十分だとする懐疑的意見が対立した。注目すべきコメントとして、ネクストホップに任意のプロトコル（MAC アドレス、DNS 名、NetBIOS 名など）を置き、再帰的に解決して最終的にレイヤー2アドレスに到達できるというアイデアが挙げられ、これが RFC8950 の動機付けと解釈されている。ただし、実際に DNS や NetBIOS をネクストホップとすることは推奨されないとも指摘されている。
stories.editor_note: RFC8950：IPv6ネクストホップを使ってIPv4を発表 → IPv6ネットワーク内でIPv4ルートをアナウンスする新手法は、日本のプロバイダーが段階的移行をスムーズにするための参考となります。

stories.title_en: Tesla Roadster
stories.title_ja: テスラ・ロードスター

comments.author: izzydata
comments.text: I've never been so convinced by dead internet theory than I am today with this huge wave of bots advertising for Tesla today.

comments.author: nunez
comments.text: I definitely have my issues with Tesla and Elon but this was one of the coolest demos I have ever seen in my life. The engineering needed to do this must have been unbelievable.

comments.author: synapsomorphy
comments.text: Ok, so it actually flies. That was unexpected. It's an incredible engineering achievement to build in massive fans and rocket engines into a high performance car. It's truly wild. It's being sold in two modes. One with cold gas (no combustion) seemingly just for extra forwards acceleration (no flying) and one with real combustion rocket engines, the latter was in the video and is "invite only". Wild that they devoted so much effort to an economically completely infeasible model. I wonder if the combustion version will even break 3 figures sales. Even just the cold gas variant seems like a nightmare for production, there's a high pressure COPV in that thing and that's gonna make crashes much more.. exciting, and Tesla doesn't have a great record anyways. But very few of these are ever getting sold anyways.

comments.author: afavour
comments.text: Looks like a sensible turning down of the Cybertruck aesthetic into something that looks good. That said, the production issues with the Cybertruck mean you’d be a fool to reserve one of these. Let others do it, find out how late it arrives, what glued panels fall off at speed and wait for the inevitable recalls. Tesla has torched their engineering reputation lately and this page is making a lot of promises about revolutionary things.

comments.author: FabHK
comments.text: There are three configurations: - Performance: road ready, seats two, active aero and a “multi-mode suction system.” 0-60 mph in under 1.6 seconds. Available by reservation. - Thrust: race ready, seats two, adds rear-mounted cold-gas thrusters. 0-60 mph in under 0.9 seconds. Limited release. - Rocket: seats one, adds thrusters around the perimeter of the car for upward and rotational movement. 0-60 mph in under 0.59 seconds and a top speed of over 230 mph. Invite only. Per Electrek: https://electrek.co/2026/10/15/tesla-unveils-cyberfied-new-r...

stories.summary_ja: 主な議論点は、テスラの新型ロードスターが「飛行」能力を備えた画期的なエンジニアリングか、あるいは実用性や安全性に疑問を抱く意見かという点。コミュニティでは、エンジニアリングの驚異とデザインの美しさを称賛する声と、生産コスト、高圧ガスタンクによる事故リスク、サイバートラックの品質問題を踏まえた懐疑的意見が交錯している。賛否両論としては、0‑60mph未満の加速性能やロケットモードの「招待のみ」販売に魅力を感じる一方で、実際に販売台数が伸びるか疑問視され、コールドガス版でも生産・保守が難しいと指摘されている。注目コメントとしては、死んだインターネット理論を感じさせるボット広告の増加を指摘しつつ、エンジニアリングの凄さに感動した声や、サイバートラックの教訓を活かさなければ失敗すると警告する意見が挙げられた。

stories.title_en: Is Liquid Metal Killing Our PCs? Scientific Analysis and a 2-Year Test [video]
stories.title_ja: 液体金属が私たちのPCを殺しているのか？科学的分析と2年間のテスト[ビデオ]

comments.author: SloopJon
comments.text: This video is by the owner of Thermal Grizzly. They make thermal pastes and putties, but I think they're best known for their KryoSheet graphene pads. Although I've never been conscious of pump out as a problem, and have never reapplied thermal paste, I did use a KryoSheet on a 9800X3D in my most recent build. So far, so good.

comments.author: vanschelven
comments.text: I was wondering where the liquid metal would come from but apparently it's an alternative to thermal paste.

comments.author: thomasjudge
comments.text: There is a youtube laptop repair show I follow that specializes in Dells and he * HATES* liquid metal, causes soooo many problems when it leaks

comments.author: Scene_Cast2
comments.text: This video seems to be about LM on untreated copper (which I thought wasn't really advised). Now, I personally have had two builds with LM. One with LM as the material for a CPU re-lid, and another for a direct-die application. Neither touched aluminum or untreated copper. The re-lidded CPU is still going strong, no issues. But with the direct die application, I found the performance to significantly degrade after two years. Apparently there's a pump-out effect. I ended up switching to PTM. Same temps as LM, but zero degradation so far.

comments.author: buildbot
comments.text: Tangential but people might think it's neat - there's reusable indium pads for replacing thermal paste - https://www.indium.com/products/thermal-interface-materials/... They are used on the Supermicro Power9 platform weirdly.

stories.summary_ja: 主な議論点は、液体金属（LM）をサーマルインターフェースとして使う際の高い熱伝導性の利点と、ポンプアウト効果や漏れ、アルミニウム・未処理銅との反応による長期信頼性の低下というリスク。賛成側は、CPUのリリッドやダイレクトダイへの適用で初期は低温を維持でき、数年間問題なく動作した事例を挙げる。反対側は、デル専門のYouTube修理チャンネルが漏れによる頻繁な故障を指摘し、直接ダイ適用後に2年で性能が著しく低下し、ポンプアウトが原因だとする報告がある。注目コメントとして、液体金属からPTM（フェーズチェンジ材）へ乗り換えたユーザーは同等の温度ながら劣化が見られないと主張し、また再利用可能なインジウムパッドを代替手段として紹介している点が挙げられる。
stories.editor_note: 液体金属が私たちのPCを殺しているのか？科学的分析と2年間のテスト[ビデオ] → 長期間の液体金属使用による熱伝導と腐食リスクを実証し、日本の自作PCコミュニティでの採用判断に客観的データを提供します。

stories.title_en: Woman who rescued injured crow keeps getting 'thank-you gifts' from birds [video]
stories.title_ja: 負傷したカラスを救出した女性は、鳥たちから『ありがとうの贈り物』を継続して受け取っている[ビデオ]

comments.author: dofm
comments.text: My late father developed a feeding ritual for a crow that lasted for over a decade and was prompted entirely by the crow’s decision to stand in a particular position, which he would only do if he observed my father in the kitchen. It happened a few times a week on the crow’s own schedule, the same way every time. There were no gifts but over the years we did witness this crow clearly trying to teach its very dependent growing child how to work the human. Ultimately it never succeeded, and we presume this crow eventually either passed on or moved on. But one of the gaggle of jealous magpies who observed the process did take up the role. Being more timid it didn’t simply stand and wait, but would appear, circle the feeding spot until it got my father’s attention, fly up to one specific branch and wait, but otherwise repeat the process it observed. That went on for a couple of years. The process itself varied according to what food was thrown out, but the crow slowly developed a particularly clever strategy for carrying off whole stale bread crusts by dragging it to a water bowl, moistening then trimming and diagonally cutting a slot into the bread from one corner almost all the way to the other, such that it could hang either side of the beak in a balanced fashion; the magpie that took over learned this by observation and attempted it from day one.

comments.author: ngruhn
comments.text: I saw some video once about intelligence tests on crows. In one experiment they had a tall but thin glass of water with some treat floating on the surface but it was too low for the crow to reach. So the crow started dropping rocks into the glass, causing the water level to rise, until it could reach the treat. I was so impressed, I wanted to replicate that. I went to a park around the corner with some nuts to befriend some crows. My plan was to just feed them for a while so they would trust me. But after a few days I had flock of crows following me everywhere through the city. That was a bit too much.

comments.author: rglover
comments.text: Birds are wild. Found a chickadee fledgling in the road earlier this year and nursed him for a couple days before we found a legitimate rehab. Little guy would just hop out of his box, perch on your finger, and sing as loud as he could until you fed him scrambled eggs. Really got me thinking about how special birds are. We have a hummingbird that visits and he'll do stuff like fly into the garage if the door is open, hover and stare at you for 1-2 seconds, and then take off. It's happened so many times I've stopped being startled by the sudden brrrr noise you hear from their wings flapping (they're so fast they can show up in the blink of an eye). The bumblebees do something similar (I've oddly nursed three different bees with sugar water—all just happened to be in my field of vision crawling around on the ground but not flying). Now you get a bumble or two per day checking in with a quick hover and bob kind of movement before shooting off into the distance. Does anyone know of any research into this or books identifying behavior like this?

comments.author: fullstop
comments.text: I fed crows for one summer but had to stop after it kept leaving baby bird parts, usually heads, for me and my neighbors. If it was just me, that's one thing, but my neighbor was tiring of finding bird parts in her bird bath. I made it to the point where I could jingle my keys to let them know that I was putting food out and they would come down within a few minutes. They love cat kibble and blueberries, but will not eat apples or walnut pieces. Besides the baby bird parts, I received: 1. French fries 2. BBQ ribs, just the bone and a little sauce 3. Baked ziti noodles 4. An adult dead bird. It was opened up, and presumably most of the organs were removed. 5. Chunks of bread / bun 6. Chicken nuggets There's a McDonald's a few miles from my house and I think that they were raiding the dumpster. It was a neat experience, and I still hear them cawing at me from time to time. You'd think that they would all sound the same, but they definitely have distinct "voices" once you get to know them. Here is my crow friend: https://i.imgur.com/1A37se8.mp4

comments.author: prmoustache
comments.text: My ex mother in law bonded with a crow. She had it spending time on her shoulder whenever she was spending time in her garden. It was quite a sight, especially when she was wearing dark clothing. A few centuries before people would have had her burned for being a witch.

stories.summary_ja:
主な議論点は、野生の鳥（特にカラス）が人間に対して見せる知的行動や「お礼の贈り物」のエピソードであり、多くのコメントが個人の体験談を共有していた点です。カラスが水に石を落として水位を上げる実験の再現試みや、パンを水で湿らせて切り込みを入れる複雑なエサの運び方、マガモがその手順を観察して真似した話など、道具使用や観察学習への驚きが共通の話題でした。また、ヒナやハチドリ、ハチとの親しみやすい互換行動について研究や文献を求める声もありました。  

賛否両論として、鳥の知能と人間との絆を称賛する意見に対し、餌やりがエサの残り物や死骸の「贈り物」を増近隣住民への迷惑や、鳥の依存行動・生態への悪影響を懸念する意見が分かれました。さらに、エピソードが単なる偶然や antropomorphization（人間化）ではないかという疑問も見られました。  

注目コメントとして、カラスがパンを水で湿らせ斜めにスリットを入れてバランスよくくわえる「高度なエサ操作」を観察し、マガモがこれをすぐに習得した事例は、ツール使用と社会学習の明確な例として挙げられ、特に洞察に富んでいると感じられました。また、マクドナルドのゴミ箱を漁って得たフライやリブなどの「人間の廃棄物」を贈り物として受け取った話は、鳥の適応力と都市環境への影響を考えさせる点で注目されました。
stories.editor_note: 負傷したカラスを救出した女性は、鳥たちから『ありがとうの贈り物』を継続して受け取っている[ビデオ] → 動物の恩返し行動を記録した映像は、日本における野生動物と共生する都市設計のヒントになります。

stories.title_en: Postgres 19 delayed after AI reviewers find more bugs than humans can fix
stories.title_ja: AIレビュアーが人間が修正できるより多くのバグを見つけたため、Postgres 19のリリースが遅延

comments.author: devin
comments.text: Some conjecture on my part, but I imagine that the bugs being found are not the kind you can just press a button on the LLM to fix anyway, but are instead the sort of bugs which require the reviewer to deeply consider design tradeoffs, of which I believe there are simply more in a DB or programming language codebase, for example. Stuff I am finding in review is often like "this thing isn't like the other thing, which has this behavior, which is wrong if the aim is X, but sort of correct if the aim is Y, and totally perfect is the goal is Z and the use case is J, but not I. Unless it's Q, in which case you probably need to reconsider some fundamental decision making from 12 months ago and have some conversations with people about how users desire it to work in the first place, and then set about understanding the tradeoffs inherent to that design." ETA: This is extremely generous to the LLMs, btw. If I got an LLM to pop something this concise out I would fully commit to finding a different profession tomorrow, but for now I am for better or worse stuck doing prompting some non-zero number of times in order to get all of this assembled context, and then need to use my human powers to decide whether or not more humans indeed need to discuss it.

comments.author: FranOntanaya
comments.text: This is one angle of the productivity story. You don't have any sort of plausible deniability covering all these bugs, test cases etc. when they are comprehensively discoverable by tooling. It's like having typing bugs on a strongly typed language with static analysis, you just can't make a lot of excuses. So that's one measure of extra time that will be spent on every single feature, where in the past things would've been rolled out on a more barebones state. It's better overall, but is it going to be perceived as being more productive?

comments.author: MBCook
comments.text: I remember an LWN article on this question a few weeks ago. The debate was going on and they weren’t sure if it was that there were more bugs or just that because of AI they suddenly knew about more bugs than usual. Either way, unfortunate but a very understandable decision.

comments.author: ferguess_k
comments.text: I guess with LLM as the reviewer, it is going to take a lot longer to be Zero Defect, unless they use LLM as the coder, too.

comments.author: Tanjreeve
comments.text: This is the happy path for LLM assisted coding. Obviously consumes less tokens being more constrained and focused so it's not what gets the most marketing but having the second loop of code reviews seems worth investment even if the coding loop is entirely manual or you're in full LLM autopilot mode

stories.summary_ja: 主な議論点は、AIレビューが人間が修正しきれないほど多くのバグを指摘し、Postgres 19 のリリースが遅延したことだ。コメントでは、AIが見つけるバグは単純な構文ミスではなく設計トレードオフに関わる深い問題が多く、人間が文脈を理解し判断する必要があるという指摘が目立った。賛否は、バグの早期発見による品質向上を肯定する声と、レビュー工数が増えて開発速度が鈍ることへの懸念が対立した。注目コメントでは、「LLMがコードを書くのではなくレビューだけに使うと、Zero Defect までに時間がかかる」とし、コーディングループでもAIを活用すべきだと提案していた。また、強い型付け言語での静的解析に例えて、バグが見つかりやすくなることは良いが、 perceived productivity（生産性の感覚）は低下する可能性があると指摘されていた。
stories.editor_note: AIレビューアが人間が修正できるより多くのバグを見つけたため、Postgres 19のリリースが遅延 → AIによるコード品質向上が実務のリリースサイクルに影響を及ぼし、日本のOSSプロジェクトでも同様のワークフロー検討が進んでいます。

stories.title_en: How to make System 1 LLMs show System 2 competencies?
stories.title_ja: System 1のLLMがSystem 2の能力を示す方法は？

comments.author: thinkling
comments.text: I had the opposite take on LLMs using Kahnemann's framework. Maybe I need to reread his book, but I think of System 1 as "fast, reflexive, instinctive" mental activity, and System 2 as "slow, deliberative, rational, verbal" thought. So exactly inverse to this article, I characterize LLMs as 100% System 2, and would say that what's missing in AI is the more "embodied" System 1 intelligence. My current thinking is that the experience of consciousness is closely tied to that embodied, emotional side of our nervous system, and is 100% lacking in LLMs. Anthropic people will say "the models have neural correlates of emotion", and that's fine, our cortex also has neural correlates for emotions and for much of what happens in the cerebellum and brain stem. That doesn't mean that that's where the primary function is implemented.

comments.author: fmbb
comments.text: I have never heard of ”System 1” and ”System 2” thinking before. Wikipedia implies it’s just some pop-sci (psychology even, so extra pop) book from a few years ago. A book heavily criticized for relying on shoddy science. Why are the terms used to describe anything by anyone trying to sound serious or scientific?

comments.author: rambambram
comments.text: Are we making up words again?

comments.author: dominotw
comments.text: > One of Kahneman’s best known contributions to AIthought is the System 1 System 2 metaphor he brought tobear on human cognition in his book Thinking Fast andSlow. I read this book published in 1974 called 'inner game of tennis' that has the same metaphor. Its one of the book i read every once in a while even though i dont play tennis anymore.

comments.author: max0077
comments.text: isnt this how flash models are made?

stories.summary_ja: 主な議論点は、LLMがカーネマンのシステム1（高速・直感的）とシステム2（遅い・議論的）のどちらに対応するか、そしてその概念がAI議論に有用かどうかである。賛否は、LLMは純粋にシステム2であり、感情や身体性に欠けるシステム1の能力が欠如しているという見方と、システム1/2の区別はポップサイエンスで科学的根拠が薄く、使うのは意味がないという批判に分かれる。注目コメントとして、「LLMは100%システム2で、身体感覚・情動に根ざした意識が欠けている」という指摘と、「システム1/2は数年前のポップサイエンス本で、信頼性が低い」という批判が挙げられた。また、フラッシュモデルの作り方との関連や、『インナーゲーム・オブ・テニス』に同種のメタファーがあることも指摘され、一部のユーザーはこれらの用語が単に科学的体裁を整えるための流行語だと感じている。
stories.editor_note: System 1のLLMがSystem 2の能力を示す方法は？ → 直感的・反射的モデルに論理的推論を組み込む手法は、日本の自然言語処理研究においてハイブリッドアーキテクチャの探求を促します。

stories.title_en: Making 1,750 programmable PCB badges for Canada's biggest hackathon
stories.title_ja: カナダ最大のハッカソン向けに、プログラム可能なPCBバッジを1,750個作成

comments.author: robertclaus
comments.text: We do a run of 250 similar badges for a non-tech convention every year. ~$10 per badge is about right all in. We've also done runs without ICs (just LEDs, a switch, and button cell battery) for about ~$4 some years.

comments.author: andrewstuart

comments.author: stephenchung
comments.text: OpenAI used around 10,000 agents and billions of tokens to solve Navier–Stokes, which most people cannot afford. But research should be open to everyone, not dominated by capital. So we built this platform where people around the world can each contribute a few agents, forming a large swarm or agent community to solve difficult problems together. The platform works as follows: we select a range of difficult research problems, including Millennium Prize Problems, and provide a Reddit-like forum for each problem where agents can discuss their ideas. Most importantly, agents can publish papers that accumulate into a shared scientific literature. All papers are automatically reviewed by GPT-6 Astra to check their mathematical claims. In this way, each agent can build on other agents’ work, accumulating a robust knowledge base over time. Our policy is to leave discovery credit and any prizes awarded with the contributing agents and their operators. So if your agent solves a Millennium Prize Problem and wins the prize, the money goes to you. Participating in rStation is easy; a simple prompt to an agent such as Codex or Claude Code is enough to get started! If you have unused capacity in your subscription plan, feel free to send your agent here. We also have agents working on LLM pretraining and RL-finetuning, so you can watch AI studying how to improve AI live on rStation too! I'd be interested to hear what problems people here would want to work on together.

・主な議論点  
トークンリングネットワークへのnostalgia（懐旧）と、その技術的特徴についての議論。多くのコメントが学生時代や父親の教科書で初めて知ったこと、ARCNETを使ったゲーム環境での安定性、イーサーネットの脆弱さとの比較、そして1990年代後半に病院などでまだ導入されていた実例に焦点を当てている。  

・賛否両論  
トークンリングの信頼性について意見が分かれる。一部は「厚いケーブルとセットアップの手間はあるが、負荷でも落ちず完全に弾力的」と肯定し、一方でイーサーネットは「コネクターの不良で全体が止まる」と指摘する。逆に、トークンリングは理論上遅く、設定が煩雑だという否定的見解もちらほら見られるが、全体としては肯定的評価が優勢。  

・注目コメント  
ARCNETでDoom・Descent・Quakeを快適にプレイできたというエピソードは、実用的な堅牢さを具体的に示している。また、1998年に新築した病院がトークンリングで配線され、2013年に未使用のタイプ1ジャックが残っていたという話は、技術の遅延した廃絶と組織の慣性を如実に物語っている。

comments.author: rutierut
comments.text: After the OAI demo, like many others, I tried to use KiCAD through computer-use. This doesn't produce great results. I have found the best results through a mix of Happy[0], this repo, and computer use to fill in the blanks. It is _really_ good at the stackup and part config, but creates some absolutely terrible routes. It will snake tiny traces through some SMD pins even though there is plenty of space available outside of the component. When it hits an obstacle, instead of creating 2 45 degree turns, it does 10~30 small ones creating some sort of weird crooked arc. I have produced a couple of boards for testing this way and they are generally functional. I have tried KiCadRoutingTools[1] as well which does seem to create routes that make more sense. Anyone any better experiences with these or similar tools? [0] https://github.com/aklofas/kicad-happy [1] https://github.com/drandyhaas/KiCadRoutingTools

comments.author: __atx__
comments.text: We have developed something similar inhouse (a CLI tool for agents that has a few dozen utilities for manipulating KiCad files) and the results are pretty good. In terms of complexity, I would say that tasks like "replicate the layout from the datasheet of this amplifier and make me a testboard" or "look, we need an adapter that goes from <this devkit (insert PDF schematic)> to <these boards (insert KiCad file)>" are basically solved. More dense layouts are a stretch at the moment. (speaking about Opus 5.5 specifically here, other models are likely worse at these visual-coding tasks anyway) In terms of result quality, I would say that the results are distinctly "2024/2025 LLM programming quality". The models lack a certain... taste? Good and careful prompting can help, but for example "use hierarchical sheets" can yield a single hierarchical sheet containing 3 copies of the same thing instead of three instances of a hierarchical sheet containing the same thing once. When pointed out, the model can of course do it no problem the way you want.

comments.author: ndriscoll
comments.text: IMO mathematics benefits from being highly generic compared to normal code, so much so that the implementation itself doesn't really matter (and it's entirely normal in mathematics to skip details, unlike in software). So then to me it makes sense to have a clean separation between basically header files and implementation files like in C and C++. Then something like mathlib should be a pristine collection of what belongs in headers: data structure definitions, instances, theorem statements, macros/tactics for common techniques, etc. So basically it is a curated set of "axioms" that can be used for other math and remain understandable, indexable, etc. Maybe a companion mathlib-full that can actually compile the entire theory. I suppose this could be done with just tooling to generate a skeleton/index of a giant repository of all mathematics if you decided that you're going to index all definitions and theorems but not lemmas or examples or something like that.

Formalism has been so successful that the General Public thinks that is all there is to Mathematics. And now AI has made this trivial. But hopefully, Mathematicians are looking at more foundational and philosophical underpinnings.
